## feature

### The remote repository now carries CI, release automation, and dependency updates

```
level: high
```

#### reason

Both workflows ran to success on the remote: the second `ci` run concluded `completed/success`, and the `release` run for `v0.1.0` concluded `completed/success` with both artifacts attached.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `ci.yml`: one job named `ci` on pushes to `main` and pull requests; Python 3.12; `pip install .[dev]`; `ruff check`, `mypy`, full `pytest` including slow tests.
2. `release.yml`: tag `v*.*.*` or manual dispatch; `python -m build` produces the sdist and wheel; a `gh` step attaches `dist/*` to the release and creates it with generated notes when missing.
3. `dependabot.yml`: `pip` and `github-actions` ecosystems, weekly, grouped.
4. Action majors were resolved from latest releases at write time (`actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/setup-python@v7`); Dependabot is the safety net.

#### before

The remote had no workflows and no dependency updates; 12 local commits, including all Phase-1 work, sat unpushed.

#### after

Pushes to `main` and pull requests run ruff, mypy, and the full pytest suite; tags build and attach release artifacts; Dependabot groups weekly updates.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`gh run list` runs 40268806314 (ci, success) and 40269237826 (release, success); `.github/workflows/{ci,release}.yml`; version queries `gh api repos/actions/checkout/releases/latest` → `v7.0.1`, `setup-python` → `v7.1.0`.

:::

## fix

### The first CI run exposed two latent test dependencies and both were fixed

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The first run failed on `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas'` and a duckdb API removal; the second run passed on the same environment after two fixes.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `tests/test_e2e.py:369` imports pandas for NaN-aware frame comparison in the cross-worker determinism test; the pixi dev env had masked the missing declaration. pandas joined the dev extra.
2. duckdb removed `Relation.fetchone()` in versions newer than the local 1.5.6; the read-back test switched to `rel.limit(1).fetchall()[0][0]`, which works across versions.
3. The failure is the value of a clean-room CI: the local environment had hidden both gaps.

#### before

`pip install .[dev]` did not install pandas, so the suite could not run in any fresh environment.

#### after

The suite runs green from a bare `pip install .[dev]` on `ubuntu-latest`.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Run 40268368638 log (`--log-failed`): the two failures quoted in the session; local `pytest tests/test_outputs_errors.py` 13 passed after the fix; run 40268806314 success.

:::

## limitation

### Branch protection cannot be applied while the repository is private on a free plan

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The protection API returned HTTP 403 with "Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature" for both PUT and GET.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The intended ruleset (context `ci`, `enforce_admins: false`, linear history, no force pushes) is recorded in the plan and must be applied at the public flip.
2. Until then, nothing enforces the `ci` check on pull requests; direct pushes to `main` remain possible by design for this solo repository.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`gh api -X PUT repos/jiangyun-fun/seqconsistency/branches/main/protection` response in the session log (403, both directions).

:::

## caveat

### The repository is not ready to flip public today; three items gate it

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The readiness scan found one infrastructure disclosure and two flip-day tasks; the secrets scan found nothing.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `pixi.toml:3` declares internal channel URLs (`file:///bioproj/tools/share/conda-jy-essentials`, `s3://conda/sibio`). No package in `pixi.lock` resolves from them, so the fix is deleting the two URLs and re-locking — mechanical, but it must happen before the flip.
2. Branch protection (item above) applies only at the flip.
3. `benchmarks/results-*.md` carry the workstation hostname (`jiangy-Precision-5820-Tower`); keep or scrub per taste.
4. Not blockers: `docs/plans` and `docs/misc` are working-session records (no credentials; a `git log -S'ghp_'` pickaxe scan over all history is clean); the Python 3.11 support claim is untested in CI (3.12 only).
5. The published sdist ships none of this: 46 files, `LICENSE` included, no `pixi.toml`, no `docs/`.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`tar tzf seqconsistency-0.1.0.tar.gz` listing (46 files); grep hits for the channel URLs limited to `pixi.toml`; empty pickaxe output for token patterns.

:::
